page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of dedicated system memory, translating to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate a strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core metrics placing it in the top 25% of tested servers. Multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench scores, and Passmark CPU evaluations generally fall within the average range. Memory bandwidth is stable, recording an average of 514.76 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 45.33 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression represents a relative bottleneck, performing in the bottom 25% of benchmarks.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated AMD EPYC hardware, this instance offers a standard resource density suitable for general-purpose workloads. It is well-suited for web serving, software compilation, and moderate database operations, as demonstrated by its average static web serving throughput of 8.25 GB/sec and stable Passmark database operation scores. It can also support lightweight machine learning tasks, such as prompt processing and text generation for small 135M parameter models.
